title: bitwise commutes with swapping the combinator's argument order
statement: For every Bool -> Bool -> Bool function f and every natural m, n: bitwise(fun a b => f(b, a), m, n) = bitwise(f, n, m).

formal.statement: ((x0 : ((x0 : Bool) -> ((x1 : Bool) -> Bool))) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.bitwise (fun (x3 : Bool) => fun (x4 : Bool) => x0 x4 x3) x1 x2) (AxNat.bitwise x0 x2 x1))))

evidence.supports: Nat.bitwise_swap is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- bitwise_swap 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.bitwise_swap[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type. `nat_theorem_inventory` exits non-zero for a name that does not exist, and `grep -Ec` consumes the pipe so the tested count decides the exit status. Anchored with `^Nat\.bitwise_swap[[:space:]]` so a sibling name cannot satisfy this row. Run `--release` -- the debug build of this inventory example SIGABRTs on stack depth (unrelated to this proof).

evidence.supports: With f = fst (fun a b => a, deliberately NON-commutative), swap(fst) = snd (fun a b => b): bitwise(swap(fst), 5, 3) = 3 and bitwise(fst, 3, 5) = 3, while the UNSWAPPED bitwise(fst, 5, 3) = 5 -- a discriminating instance where m != n and f is not commutative, so a vacuous test built from and/or/xor (all commutative) could not have caught a transposed swap.
evidence.notes: Applies `Nat.bitwise_swap` symbolically (against free `m`, `n` at a fixed concrete `f = fst_fn`) and at the concrete instance `(m, n) = (5, 3)`, confirming both that the admitted type matches `Eq (bitwise (swap fst) 5 3) (bitwise fst 3 5)` and that the swapped/unswapped values genuinely differ (3 vs 5), so the instance is non-vacuous.

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*); `x0` is `f`, `x1`/`x2` are `m`/`n`, and the inline lambda `fun x3 x4 => x0 x4 x3` is `Function.swap f`.

Simpler than `Nat.bitwise_comm` (`F:nat-bitwise-comm`), and worth recording why: `swap f` applied to any two `Bool`s beta-reduces DIRECTLY to `f` applied to them in the other order, because the swap is baked into which function gets applied rather than asserted about a fixed one. So `bitwise_swap` needs NO hypothesis on `f` at all -- every site `bitwise_comm` needed `hf : forall a b, f a b = f b a` plus a propositional `Bool` congruence for (the two boundary rows and the per-bit combine) is pure defeq here. Confirmed by hand (case-by-case substitution, not Python -- the recursion is small enough to trace directly) before writing any Rust: expanding `bitwiseAux (swap f) fuel m n` and `bitwiseAux f fuel n m` matches by beta/iota alone in every case except the both-nonzero recursive step, which needs exactly the induction hypothesis (the per-bit `bit` term there also matches the other side exactly, by the same beta-swap, so only the recursive sub-call needs a `d.congr`).

Two new lemmas land in `nat_prelude/bitwise.rs` (uncontended at landing time): `bitwise_aux_swap_of_fuel` (fuel induction, `Le m fuel -> Le n fuel -> ...`, no `hf` needed) and `bitwise_swap` (assembled through the shared fuel `m + n`, reusing the ALREADY-DECLARED `bitwise_aux_agree_of_fuel` from `bitwise_comm`'s own dispatch, exactly as `bitwise_comm`'s own final assembly).

This is the `Nat.bitwise` twin of Mathlib v4.30's `Nat.bitwise_swap` (`F:ml430-nat-bitwise-swap-7175e90e`, flipped alongside this fact) -- our `Nat.bitwise` is Mathlib's OWN general combinator (not a specialization), so this closes the same proposition Mathlib states, restated pointwise because this kernel has no `funext` to state Mathlib's `Function.swap`-level function equality directly (the same restatement convention used throughout this prelude, e.g. `nat_prelude/cantor.rs`'s module doc).
